questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'He is ___ honest and dedicated officer.'
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a silent 'h' and a vowel phoneme /ɒ/, requiring the indefinite article 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'She has enrolled in ___ university in Islamabad.'
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a consonant glide sound /juː/ (like 'yoo'), thus taking the indefinite article 'a' rather than 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article for acronyms: 'His brother is ___ MBA graduate from a prestigious business school.'
questions.explanation: The abbreviation 'MBA' is pronounced starting with a vowel phoneme /ɛm/, thus requiring the indefinite article 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'I met ___ one-eyed beggar near the railway crossing.'
questions.explanation: 'One-eyed' begins with the consonantal labio-velar glide /w/ sound (like 'won'), taking 'a' (e.g., 'a one-eyed man').

questions.question: Select the correct sentence regarding geographical article usage:

options.A: The Himalayas form the northern boundary of South Asia.
options.B: The Mount Everest is the highest mountain peak in the world.
options.C: The Asia is the largest continent on Earth.
options.D: The Lake Saif-ul-Malook is in Kaghan.

questions.explanation: Mountain ranges (chains) take the definite article 'the' ('The Himalayas', 'The Alps'), whereas individual mountain peaks ('Mount Everest', 'K2') do not take an article.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He is addicted ___ smoking.'
questions.explanation: The adjective 'addicted' takes the dependent preposition 'to'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The candidate was accused ___ forgery.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'accused' strictly governs the preposition 'of' ('accused of a crime').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'I prefer reading classical literature ___ watching television.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to' (never 'than') when expressing preference between two gerunds or nouns.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The committee agreed ___ my proposed plan.'
questions.explanation: One agrees 'with' a person, but agrees 'to' a proposal, suggestion, or plan.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'You must abide ___ the rules and regulations of the institution.'
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'abide by' means to accept and comply with a rule or decision.

questions.question: Select the correct sentence with proper article usage:

options.A: The Holy Quran is the final divine revelation.
options.B: Holy Quran is final divine revelation.
options.C: A Holy Quran is the final revelation.
options.D: The Holy Quran is a final divine revelation.

questions.explanation: Holy scriptures take the definite article 'the' ('The Holy Quran', 'The Bible').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He congratulated his friend ___ securing the top position.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'congratulate' takes the dependent preposition 'on' (or 'upon'), not 'for'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The old merchant is blind ___ the faults of his son.'
questions.explanation: 'Blind in/of' one eye refers to physical sight deficiency, while 'blind to' denotes figurative unawareness or refusal to acknowledge faults.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'Karachi is ___ Manchester of Pakistan.'
questions.explanation: When a proper noun ('Manchester') is used as a common noun for comparison/analogy, it takes the definite article 'the'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He jumped ___ the swimming pool to rescue the child.'
questions.explanation: 'Into' conveys dynamic motion from outside to an interior enclosed space, unlike the static preposition 'in'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'We have been waiting for the bus ___ two hours.'
questions.explanation: 'For' is used to indicate an extent or duration of time ('two hours'), whereas 'since' denotes a specific starting point in time.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He has been studying in this school ___ 2020.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' specifies the exact point in past time ('2020') from which an action commenced.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'This post is senior ___ that one in the administrative hierarchy.'
questions.explanation: Comparative adjectives ending in '-ior' (senior, junior, superior, inferior) are always followed by 'to'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The little girl takes ___ her mother in both looks and temperament.'
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'take after' means to resemble a parent or ancestor in appearance or behavior.

questions.question: Select the correct article: '___ higher you ascend, ___ cooler it becomes.'
questions.explanation: Parallel double comparative structures showing proportional increase or decrease take 'the...the' ('The higher...the cooler').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The patient died ___ cholera during the epidemic.'
questions.explanation: One dies 'of' a specific direct disease (e.g., 'died of cholera', 'died of cancer'), but dies 'from' an external cause like wounds, overwork, or loss of blood.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'He is ___ European tourist visiting the northern valleys.'
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with the phonetic semi-vowel consonant sound /j/ (yoo-ro-pean), requiring the indefinite article 'a'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He insisted ___ accompanying me to the airport.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'insist' is followed by the preposition 'on' (or 'upon') and a gerund ('insisted on accompanying').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: '___ Indus is the longest river in Pakistan.'
questions.explanation: Names of rivers always take the definite article 'the' ('The Indus', 'The Nile', 'The Amazon').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The detective looked ___ the suspicious financial transaction.'
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'look into' means to investigate or examine thoroughly.

questions.question: Choose the sentence where the article is CORRECTLY OMITTED (Zero Article):

options.B: The gold is a precious metal.
options.D: An gold is the precious metal.

questions.explanation: Material and abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article ('Gold is a precious metal').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'She is exceptionally good ___ mathematics.'
questions.explanation: The adjective 'good' indicating proficiency or skill pairs with the preposition 'at' ('good at mathematics', 'good at sports').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'She has been appointed as ___ SP in Punjab Police.'
questions.explanation: The abbreviation 'SP' begins with vowel phoneme /ɛs/ ('es-pee'), requiring the indefinite article 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He was deprived ___ all his ancestral property.'
questions.explanation: 'Deprived' is followed by the preposition 'of'.

questions.question: Select the correct sentence with proper article usage for countries:

options.A: He currently resides in the United States.
options.B: He currently resides in the Pakistan.
options.C: He currently resides in the China.
options.D: He currently resides in a United States.

questions.explanation: Countries whose formal names are plural or contain political nouns (Kingdom, Republic, States) take 'the' ('The United States', 'The United Kingdom', 'The UAE').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'Are you eligible ___ this merit scholarship?'
questions.explanation: The adjective 'eligible' takes the dependent preposition 'for'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'We should not laugh ___ the misfortunes of others.'
questions.explanation: 'Laugh at' is the standard prepositional verb denoting derision or mocking.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate article: 'Man is ___ mortal being.'
questions.explanation: 'Mortal' begins with a consonant sound /m/, taking the indefinite article 'a'.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He was confident ___ winning the regional debate.'
questions.explanation: 'Confident' takes the preposition 'of' followed by a gerund ('confident of winning').

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'The train arrived exactly ___ time.'
questions.explanation: 'On time' means punctual / strictly according to schedule, whereas 'in time' means early enough before a deadline.
